Bill.BriefDescription: Providing procedures for resolving boundary disputes.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to procedures for resolving boundary disputes; andamending RCW 58.04.020.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 58.04.020 and 1996 c 160 s 8 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Whenever the boundaries of lands between two or more adjoiningproprietors have been lost, or by time, accident or any other cause,have become obscure, or uncertain, and the adjoining proprietors cannotagree to establish the same, one or more of the adjoining proprietorsmay bring a civil action in equity, in the superior court, for thecounty in which such lands, or part of them are situated, and thatsuperior court, as a court of equity, may upon the complaint, ordersuch lost or uncertain boundaries to be erected and established andproperly marked. (2) The superior court may order the parties to utilize mediationbefore the civil action is allowed to proceed. (3) In an action brought under this section, the superior court maygrant injunctive relief or other temporary restraining orders toprevent the removal of, or damages to, property located on the portion p. 1 HB 1122of land that is in dispute. The court may grant such relief whether ornot the parties are required to utilize mediation before the civilaction is allowed to proceed. The court may also grant such reliefwithout the requesting party being required to post bond if the courtfinds there exists a likelihood that the requesting party will prevailon the merits of the action brought under this section. The courtshall require a party who violates the order for injunctive relief ortemporary restraining order to pay damages to the injured party.Nothing in this subsection impairs, modifies, or supplants any otherremedy available at law or equity.
